text.p: Pancontinental Mining Ltd said on Wednesday production from its Paddington gold mine rose 29 percent to 38,197 ounces in the December quarter compared to the year earlier period, when teething problems occurred at processing plant.

Second quarter production from the plant fell three percent from the previous quarter, however, due to poor recoveries from oxide material mined in the bridge area of the mine's two pits, the company said.
For the six months, production was 79,048 ounces versdus 42,924 ounces in the year earlier period, Pancontinental said.
Unit cash costs were A$506 per ounce for the quarter and A$455 per ounce in the half-year respectively, the company said.
The costs compared with A$533 and A$594 per ounce in the corresponding year earlier periods.
The Paddington processing plant exceeded nameplate capacity during the quarter and year to date period, despite treating a blend containing more sulphide ore than anticipated, Pancontinental said.
A total of 795,205 tonnes, grading 1.7 grammes of gold per tonne was treated, with a 87 percent recovery rate, it said.
For the six months, 1,578,181 tonnes at 1.7 grams gold were treated with an average recovery of 89 percent, the company said.
Mining continued according to schedule in Phases 2 and 3 of the Paddington Stage 3 expansion, the company said.
Development of a dewatering decline under Paddington I is largely complete and construction of the pumping facility had commenced, Pancontinental said.

Gold mineralisation intersected in the decline confirmed the continuation of the Paddington I orebody. A diamond drilling program was planned to test the extent of this mineralisation at depth, it said.

The company said its Kundana mine produced 22,452 ounces at an average cash cost of A$370 per ounce during the December quarter and 46,925 ounces at A$338 per ounce for the six months. This compared with 27,182 ounces at A$245 per ounce and 52,976 ounces at A$252 per ounce for the respective corresponding periods in 1995.
Pancontinental is 87.71 percent owned by Goldfields Ltd
